title: VeriHGN: Heterogeneous Graph-Based Congestion Prediction for Chip Layout Verification

problem.claim: VLSI layout verification faces increasing difficulty as designs grow in size and complexity, while accurate congestion identification requires detailed routing and therefore makes traditional verification time-consuming and costly.

gap.claim: Prior learning-based methods often loosely couple netlist connectivity with layout features and primarily produce numerical congestion estimates.

contributions.claim: A verification framework named VeriHGN is proposed using an enhanced heterogeneous graph that jointly represents circuit components and spatial grids.
The framework models interactions between logical intent and physical realization through a unified relational representation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On industrial benchmarks including ISPD2015, CircuitNet-N14, and CircuitNet-N28, VeriHGN is reported to achieve the best or near-best performance among state-of-the-art methods on prediction accuracy and correlation metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: VLSI scaling increases the challenge of layout verification in EDA workflows.
Congestion is accurately identifiable only after detailed routing, increasing verification cost and time.
Learning-based approaches seek earlier congestion prediction, but existing methods loosely couple logical and physical features.
VeriHGN uses a unified heterogeneous graph to represent circuit components, spatial grids, and their interactions.
Experiments on three industrial benchmarks report best or near-best performance on accuracy and correlation metrics.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative metric values, evaluation splits, or baseline details.
The abstract does not specify the congestion target representation or prediction horizon.
The abstract does not report computational cost or routing-iteration reductions.
